_readme: Content for the dashboard's Notable Views tab. Each 'view' is a short paraphrase of a public statement (quotes are verbatim), with a link to where it was said and the date. Every entry must be checked against its source by a human before publishing. Views are grouped on the page by 'topic' (ids from the topics list). 'check' names a live comparison in dashboard_site/index.html (ANALYST_CHECKS); views on the same check within a topic share one data reading. 'horizon' says which window the check measures over, matching how far ahead the view looks: 'near' (today's reading), 'direction' (12-month change), 'structural' (multi-year averages/trends). the page flags any person whose views_as_of is more than 60 days old. Refresh cadence: the day after each FOMC meeting (views often expire with the meeting).

analysts.name: Ray Dalio
analysts.lens: Long-term debt cycles: when government debt outgrows the ability to service it, the endgame is higher rates or money printing, and hard assets like gold outperform.

themes.view: Says the government's finances are "at an inflection point" and a debt crisis could come in about three years, "give or take two," if the course isn't changed.

source.title: CNBC, on his LinkedIn post

analysts.name: Ritesh Jain
analysts.lens: Global liquidity and capital flows: financial repression keeps rates below inflation, the dollar weakens, and real assets beat financial ones.

themes.view: "Long yields are revolting earlier than I expected." Calls long-duration Western government bonds "certificates of confiscation" under financial repression.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: The 30- and 10-year yields would both need to be up at least a quarter point over the past 12 months.

themes.view: Expects US inflation to settle at 3–4% rather than below 2% — "a view rather than something anyone can verify today."

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: CPI inflation would need to average 3% or more a year over three years, and markets' long-run inflation expectation (the 5-year rate starting five years out) would need to reach 2.5% or more.

themes.view: "I expect the economy to weaken from the fourth quarter" of 2026, as tax and tariff support fades.

themes.view: Heavy government borrowing and the demand for capital to build AI keep pressure on yields, "arguing against the likelihood of a decline in interest rates anytime soon."

source.title: Oaktree memo — Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics, Part III

themes.if_differs: The 10-year yield would need to run above its 10-year average while the term premium rises.

themes.view: "Inflation is stubbornly higher than is desirable," citing PCE inflation of 3.7% in July against the Fed's 2% target.

source.title: Oaktree memo — Shall We Repeal the Laws of Economics, Part III

themes.if_differs: Core inflation over the last three months would need to run at 3% a year or more, or above its 12-month rate.

themes.view: Markets are "heavily reliant on a single factor: the success of AI." Lenders "will have to be exceptionally vigilant regarding the creditworthiness of the borrowers they back."

analysts.name: Claudia Sahm
analysts.role: Macroeconomist; creator of the Sahm Rule; former Federal Reserve economist
analysts.lens: The labor market and recessions: what the jobs data says about where the economy is headed, and what the Fed should do about it.

themes.view: Agrees with the two October dissenters who wanted a rate hike, and says a gradual approach "should translate into a quarter-point hike in December."

source.title: Stay-At-Home Macro — What will it take to be confident about inflation?

themes.if_differs: Core inflation over the last three months would need to run at 3% a year or more, or above its 12-month rate.

themes.view: "The labor market has remained in balance": "unemployment is low and stable."

source.title: Stay-At-Home Macro — What will it take to be confident about inflation?

themes.if_differs: Unemployment would need to be within about a third of a point of its level a year ago, with the Sahm Rule in its normal range.
